test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 19 Sept 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
This question is based on the five, four-digit numbers given below.

(Left) 6338 5345 4127 7253 6176 (Right)

(Example: 697 – first digit = 6, second digit = 9, third digit = 7)

(NOTE: All operations to be done from left to right)

If 3 is subtracted from the first digit of every number, in how many numbers will the first digit be exactly divisible by 3?
solution:
Given: (left) 6338 5345 4127 7253 6176 (right)

If 3 is subtracted from the first digit of every number:

 
• 6338: 6 - 3 = 3
 
• 5345: 5 - 3 = 2
 
• 4127: 4 - 3 = 1
 
• 7253: 7 - 3 = 4
 
• 6176: 6 - 3 = 3

Now checking which of these new first digits are exactly divisible by 3:

 
• 3 (divisible by 3)
 
• 2 (not divisible by 3)
 
• 1 (not divisible by 3)
 
• 4 (not divisible by 3)
 
• 3 (divisible by 3)

The number of first digits that are exactly divisible by 3 is: 2

The correct answer is "Option 2".
